module: People's rights: what customers and staff can ask for

lesson.title: Portability and the right to object
lesson.summary: Decide when data portability applies, and handle general and direct-marketing objections.

prerequisites.reason: Portability depends on processing based on consent or contract.
The general objection targets processing based on legitimate interests or public tasks.

blocks: **Data portability** (Article 20(1)): a person may receive the personal data **they provided** in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format, and transmit it to another controller without hindrance. It applies only where:

items: processing is based on **consent** or a **contract**; and
processing is carried out by **automated means**.

blocks: Where technically feasible, the person may have the data sent **directly** to another controller (Article 20(2)).

Portability does not apply where the basis is a public task (Article 20(3)) or a legal obligation (recital 68). Controllers are not obliged to adopt technically compatible systems (recital 68). The right must not adversely affect others (Article 20(4)).
**The right to object** (Article 21(1)): a person may object, on grounds relating to their **particular situation**, to processing based on a **public task or legitimate interests**.
The controller must then stop, unless it demonstrates **compelling legitimate grounds** that override the person's interests, rights and freedoms, or needs the data for legal claims.
**Direct marketing** (Article 21(2)-(3)): a person may object **at any time**. Then the data **must no longer be processed** for marketing.
There is no balancing test here, and recital 70 says the objection is free of charge.
The right to object must be **explicitly brought to the person's attention** at the latest at the first communication, presented clearly and separately from other information (Article 21(4)).

items: A customer wants her pre-order history in a file she can upload to another app. The data is processed under a contract, by automated means, so portability applies.
An employee objects to a camera covering her workstation, which relies on legitimate interests. Sunfield must stop, unless it can show compelling grounds that override hers.
A customer objects to marketing emails. Sunfield stops sending them, with no balancing.

blocks.text: These Sunfield examples are **illustrations**. A real assessment depends on all the facts.

questions.prompt: An employee asks for her salary-tax data under the portability right. The basis is a legal obligation. Does portability apply?

options.blocks: No, it applies only to consent or contract
options.reason: Article 20(1)(a) and recital 68.

options.blocks: Yes, portability applies to all personal data
options.reason: It is limited to consent or contract, by automated means.

options.blocks: Yes, if the data is kept on paper
options.reason: Portability also requires automated processing.

variants.prompt: Is portability available when the legal basis is a legal obligation?

options.blocks: Yes, portability applies to all personal data
options.reason: It is limited to consent or contract, by automated means.

options.blocks: Yes, if the data is kept on paper
options.reason: Portability also requires automated processing.

options.blocks: No, it applies only to consent or contract
options.reason: Article 20(1)(a) and recital 68.

questions.prompt: In what form must ported data be provided?

options.blocks: A printed copy sent by post
options.reason: Paper is not machine-readable.

options.blocks: Screenshots of the account pages
options.reason: Images are not a structured, machine-readable format.

options.blocks: Structured, commonly used and machine-readable
options.reason: Article 20(1).

questions.prompt: A customer objects to Sunfield's marketing emails. May Sunfield keep sending them if its interest is strong?

options.blocks: Only after she explains her reasons
options.reason: No reasons are needed for a marketing objection.

options.blocks: No, it must stop marketing to her
options.reason: Article 21(3): no further processing for marketing.

options.blocks: Yes, if its interest is compelling
options.reason: The compelling-grounds test applies to general objections, not marketing.

variants.prompt: After a customer objects to direct marketing, may Sunfield weigh its interests against hers?

options.blocks: No, it must stop marketing to her
options.reason: Article 21(3): no further processing for marketing.

options.blocks: Yes, if its interest is compelling
options.reason: The compelling-grounds test applies to general objections, not marketing.

options.blocks: Only after she explains her reasons
options.reason: No reasons are needed for a marketing objection.

questions.prompt: An employee objects to a camera on her workstation, which relies on legitimate interests. What follows?

options.blocks: Stop, unless compelling grounds override hers
options.reason: Article 21(1).

options.blocks: Nothing; objection applies only to consent-based processing
options.reason: Article 21(1) targets public-task and legitimate-interest processing.

options.blocks: Stop at once, with no exception possible
options.reason: Article 21(1) allows compelling grounds and legal claims.

options.blocks: Nothing; objection applies only to consent-based processing
options.reason: Article 21(1) targets public-task and legitimate-interest processing.
